adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~255 (updateEvent) — When externalCalendarId is undefined (legacy bookings), `event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)` finds nothing and `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined })` sends an invalid request to Google, breaking reschedule/update of legacy bookings

adjudication.rationale:
In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts deleteEvent, the fallback logic was changed from using the event’s destination calendar externalId to a self-referential find:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/falsy, the code searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === undefined`, which will typically return `undefined` even if the event actually has a valid destination calendar. That makes `calendarId` undefined and (given the immediately preceding `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`) the request will fall back to deleting from `primary` instead of the real calendar, risking orphaned events. This is a concrete defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:253,315 — broken fallback predicate: cal.externalId === undefined never matches, causing undefined calendarId and Google API 404 on reschedule/delete

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch is:

- updateEvent: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`
- deleteEvent: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the case where a fallback is needed), the `find` predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, which typically matches nothing (destination calendars normally have an externalId). That makes the fallback evaluate to `undefined`, so the request may be sent without a valid calendarId (or fall back incorrectly if later code doesn’t handle it). These changes do remove the prior implicit ownership invariant (only using credentials already associated with the user/loaded set) and are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destinationCalendar?.find comparing cal.externalId === externalCalendarId when externalCalendarId is falsy always yields undefined in CalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, orphaning Google calendar events on reschedule/cancel (P2)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar ID as:

- `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g. `null`/`undefined`), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. `=== null/undefined`, which will almost always return no match and thus `undefined`. This is verifiable from the diff.

This is likely reachable because `EventManager.updateBooking` sets `calenderExternalId: string | null = null` and passes it through (`updateEvent(..., calenderExternalId)`), so `externalCalendarId` can indeed be null. Result: Google update/delete can be attempted with an undefined/incorrect `calendarId`, causing failures or acting on the wrong calendar, which can leave the original event undeleted/unchanged (i.e., effectively orphaned on reschedule/cancel).
